messages:
sam: Heads up — deploy-bot just flagged a post-canary p95 latency spike for release v3.6.0. Deploy window still open but we have some Dedicated customers on the path. Thoughts?

deploy-bot: Auto-trigger threshold crossed: p95 > 500ms for 3m across canary slice. Suggested action: autorevert to v3.5.2. Reason: increased tail latency and 502s in frontend.

nina: Where are the 502s coming from? infra or model timeout?

rahul: Looking at the canary logs, a lot of requests hit kv-cache miss + model quantization fallback. Could be a kernel path regression.

elaine: If we autorevert we need to notify Dedicated customers — they expect stable pinned versions. Do we have a pin in place?

sam: No pin for this rollout. Change window is still open for another 22m. I don't love an automatic revert without ops signoff for Dedicated. Can we hold and do a manual targeted rollback for the canary traffic first?

oncall-bot: @sam acknowledged. Holding auto-rollback for 10 minutes per operator hold. Please escalate if degradation continues.

deploy-bot: Note: holding auto-rollback will suppress further autoreverts for this thread. Manual actions recommended: 1) run smoke tests on canary hosts; 2) if confirmed, rollback canary slice or pin to 3.5.2; 3) if larger rollback required, follow release rollback playbook.

rahul: I'm running a quick smoke now. Sharing a trimmed log snippet:
```
[2026-03-23T12:01:02Z] svc-front: upstream 10.0.5.12:502 error 502 Bad Gateway
[2026-03-23T12:01:03Z] inference-runtime: kvcache miss -> quant fallback -> latency 620ms
[2026-03-23T12:01:04Z] model-kern: selected fallback kernel: fp16->int8
```

nina: That latency sample matches the p95 bump. If it's a quant fallback, a kernel flag could fix it, but that's risky mid-window.

elaine: Proposed plan: 1) Manual rollback of canary slice to v3.5.2 (no full release revert yet). 2) Pin dedicated customer routes to 3.5.2 for safety. 3) Draft comms for affected customers. 4) Post-mortem + rollback root cause.

sam: +1 for targeted canary rollback and pins. Who will run the rollback and customer pin? rahul?

rahul: I can run the canary rollback. Command I'll use:
```
# rollback canary slice
redwoodctl rollout rollback --service=inference --to-version=3.5.2 --slice=canary --reason="p95 spike post-canary"
# pin dedicated route
redwoodctl routes pin --route=dedicated-eu --version=3.5.2
```

elaine: Also prepare a one-paragraph customer note: "We observed increased latency for a canary subset after the v3.6.0 rollout. We are rolling the canary back and pinning dedicated routes to the prior stable release while we investigate. No action required from customers; we’ll follow up with a detailed report."

sam: Nice. QA: please run the expanded smoke after rollback and confirm p95 back to baseline. If not, escalate to full rollback.

rahul: Executing canary rollback now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: rahul initiated rollback at 2026-03-23T12:06:15Z. Rollback job id: rb-20260323-1721

rahul: Rollback completed on canary slice. Running smoke.

rahul: Smoke results: p95 back to 120ms, 502s gone from canary logs.

nina: Verified telemetry graphs look normal for canary. Good call holding auto-rollback.

elaine: Draft sent to CS & AE teams for Dedicated customers. Copy of comms below: 
```
Subject: Brief: canary rollback during deployment v3.6.0
Hi — during a canary rollout we observed increased tail latency affecting a small subset of traffic. We have rolled the canary back to v3.5.2 and pinned Dedicated routes as a precaution. No customer action required. We’ll share a deeper post-mortem within 48 hours.
```

sam: Thanks team. Next steps: 1) Engineering triage on kernel selection/quant fallback. 2) Decide whether to reattempt v3.6.0 with a hotfix or wait next scheduled window. 3) Post-mortem + changelog update (release notes update: mark v3.6.0 paused).

rahul: I'll open the post-mortem ticket and attach logs + rollback command. I'll keep the canary pinned for 1h then handback to deploybot for next attempt.

deploy-bot: Rollback recorded. Recommend disabling the risky kernel flag for next candidate builds.

sam: Closing thread for now. If anything regresses, ping this thread or @oncall. :thumbsup:
